pathway.title: CHARLES RIVER LABORATORIES INTERNATIONAL, INC. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The recovery in demand is real and is led by the largest segment, so the operating trend now supports credit quality. Organic revenue growth moved from down 1.5% in the first quarter to up 0.1% in the second and up 4.7% in the third, discovery and safety assessment grew 5.9% organically in the third quarter on higher regulated study volume, its backlog rose to $2.0 billion from $1.9 billion at the year-end, and management raised its 2026 organic growth guidance by 150 basis points in August and by 100 basis points in November. Management attributes the third-quarter non-GAAP operating margin of 23.0%, against 19.7% a year earlier, to operating leverage on higher study volume and to the sale of the loss-making contract manufacturing business known as CDMO, so some of the gain is portfolio change and not demand. Reported revenue is still guided to fall 1.5% to 2.0% in 2026 because of the May divestitures, and the guidance and backlog are management measures. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-07_crl1q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_crl2q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_crl3q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation P1

Underlying earning power is stable but reported earnings are distorted by charges that recur, so neither the reported nor the adjusted measure is a safe anchor on its own. EBITDA before impairments was 21.13% of revenue in FY2024, 21.23% in FY2025 and 21.60% over the last twelve months, while the reported operating margin fell from 5.6% to 0.6% between FY2024 and FY2025, mainly because intangible asset impairments of USD 210,974 thousand arrived on top of goodwill impairments of USD 215,000 thousand in FY2024 and USD 165,000 thousand in FY2025. Restructuring charges of $107.0 million, $99.8 million and $73.8 million in FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026 show that cost programmes are a running cost, and 2026 operating income also holds a $38.5 million property gain and a $44.6 million reserve release, together $83.1 million or 18.78% of nine-month operating income, that will not repeat. Basis: calculation F2; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_crl3q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash conversion is solid and capital intensity is moderate, but 2026 conversion is weaker than the headline suggests. Free cash flow of USD 518,494 thousand in FY2025 was 60.82% of EBITDA before impairments, capital expenditure was 5.46% of revenue, and over the last twelve months free cash flow of USD 399,634 thousand was 16.33% of total debt. In the first nine months of 2026 free cash flow fell 25.84% to USD 341,064 thousand on bonus payments and professional fees, and cash paid for income taxes fell by USD 57,048 thousand to USD 35,643 thousand, which helped operating cash flow; whether the lower tax payments repeat is not established. Basis: calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 46; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Financial policy is the main credit risk, because 2026 spending on acquisitions and buybacks has outrun free cash flow. In the first nine months free cash flow of USD 341,064 thousand covered only 37.78% of the USD 902,753 thousand spent on acquisitions, deferred consideration and buybacks, disposal and insurance proceeds filled part of the gap, the revolver rose from USD 616,503 thousand at the year-end to USD 943,174 thousand after a first-quarter peak of USD 1,165,073 thousand, and net debt rose USD 320,214 thousand. In FY2025 buybacks of $350.0 million were 67.50% of free cash flow, so the change is the acquisition programme. Net leverage on EBITDA before impairments rose from 2.26x to 2.61x, all $300.0 million of programme buybacks were made in the first two quarters, and $700.0 million of authorisation remains, so resumption while the revolver is drawn is the event that would turn this finding into a downgrade of the view. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F6; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_crl2q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Liquidity is adequate and no material debt falls due before fiscal 2028, so the credit test is the 2028 to 2029 refinancing and not the next twelve months. Cash of USD 200,381 thousand and undrawn revolver commitments of USD 1,056,826 thousand give USD 1,257,207 thousand, or USD 1,235,507 thousand if the $21.7 million of letters of credit use the facility, and the ladder printed at the year-end shows only USD 2,883 thousand of principal before fiscal 2028. Fiscal 2028 holds the 2028 notes of USD 500,000 thousand and fiscal 2029 holds the revolver and the 2029 notes at USD 1,443,174 thousand, which is 1.68x EBITDA before impairments. The weighted average interest rate is 4.11% and the three series of notes carry fixed coupons of 4.25%, 3.75% and 4.00%, while the revolver margin is set by the leverage ratio, so rising leverage raises its cost; the files give no rating or market yield, so the cost of refinancing the notes is not established. Basis: calculation F8; calculation F9; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 153; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The covenant tests cannot be turned into headroom, and reported ratios conflict with the stated compliance. The credit agreement requires EBITDA less capital expenditure to cash interest of at least 3.50x and debt to EBITDA of no more than 4.25x on contract definitions, and the company stated compliance at 2025-12-27. On reported EBITDA the ratios at that date were 2.06x and 4.99x, outside both levels, so contract EBITDA must add back items such as impairments by an amount the files do not give, and no compliance statement is printed for 2026. Availability of the revolver, which is secured on substantially all assets of the company, is therefore the main dependency of the liquidity view. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 152; calculation F12; calculation P3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Competition, animal-testing policy and primate supply cap growth and pricing but do not threaten near-term cash flow. The company competes with the in-house resources of its clients and with described rivals in each segment, many contracts are fixed price or capped fee-for-service so overruns fall on the company, and in many cases it is owed no termination fee if a client cancels. The FDA announced in April 2025 that it would expand the use of new approach methodologies in preclinical safety studies and the company describes the move away from animal testing as gradual over many years, while primate supply rests on a limited source that the January 2026 Cambodian acquisition partly internalises. These risks lower the quality of the revenue base slowly, and in FY2025 a 2.0% fall in discovery and safety assessment revenue cost 37.10% of the lost revenue in segment operating income, a figure that includes higher restructuring charges. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation F13

Claims outside the debt figure are moderate against cash flow, but they add fixed charges that sit ahead of equity. Operating lease commitments were $626.6 million at the year-end with $80.7 million due within twelve months, unconditional purchase obligations were about $340 million, the company may fund up to $45.0 million of losses and capital expenditure of the divested CDMO business, the Noveprim minority holders hold a put carried at USD 43,173 thousand, and the net pension and supplemental plan liability was USD 32,170 thousand. None is in the debt figure, so lease and purchase commitments should be read with interest cover of 4.32x on reported EBITDA. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation P4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Headline 2026 profit overstates cash earnings and should not drive the view. Net income of USD 318,882 thousand for the first nine months includes a non-cash reversal of acquired tax reserves of USD 245,638 thousand, of which $44.6 million sits in operating income and about $201 million in the tax line, leaving USD 73,244 thousand, which is itself after a $181.7 million pre-tax loss on the CDMO and Cell Solutions sale that sits in other expense, outside operating income and EBITDA. The credit view therefore rests on cash flow and EBITDA, not on reported earnings per share. Basis: calculation F10; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 45; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_crl3q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_crl3q26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Five strengths support the view, in order of weight. Demand and backlog are recovering in the largest segment, and semi-fixed laboratory cost means extra volume lifts margin and free cash flow, which supports deleveraging capacity. Client and geographic diversification mean that no client was above 4% of revenue and no client above 8% of any segment, so the loss of one client cannot break cash flow. Free cash flow of USD 518,494 thousand in FY2025 on capital expenditure of 5.46% of revenue funds interest and shareholder returns internally. Liquidity of USD 1,257,207 thousand and the absence of material maturities before 2028 give time to refinance. Management has moved to sell loss-making units and to cut costs, with about $300 million of annualised savings targeted by the end of 2026, which improves the quality of earnings if the savings are realised. Basis: calculation F5; calculation F8; calculation P1; calculation P2; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 36

Five weaknesses constrain the view, in order of weight. Financial policy has put acquisitions and buybacks ahead of debt reduction, which lifted net leverage on EBITDA before impairments from 2.26x to 2.61x in nine months. Reported total debt to EBITDA of 5.51x and the unresolved gap to the covenant definition leave headroom not calculable. Impairments and restructuring recur, so reported earnings are low in quality. Debt is concentrated in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029, with the revolver, secured on substantially all assets, maturing in December 2029. Regulatory pressure on animal testing, limited primate supply and fixed-price contracts erode pricing power slowly, and the fall in discovery and safety assessment revenue in FY2025 showed that cost does not flex fully. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F6; calculation F12; calculation F9; calculation F13

On the nine dimensions of financial profile, scale and market position is Strong because the company states that it is the largest provider in its field and reports USD 4,015,382 thousand of revenue, although market share is not established; business diversification is Strong by client and geography but Average by end market because demand rests on drug research funding; competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability, ability to refinance, liquidity position and financial policy and governance are each Average; none is Weak. Financial policy and governance is the weakest dimension in the sense of the greatest credit uncertainty, because the files show no creditor-adverse conduct but nothing that commits management to deleveraging. The six business quality factors follow the same pattern: revenue durability, margin resilience, free cash flow conversion, liquidity buffer and refinancing capacity are Average and governance and financial policy is Average with a negative bias, and the primary downside path is renewed client funding restraint during the revolver-funded acquisition and buyback programme ahead of the fiscal 2028 to 2029 maturities. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation F1; calculation F12; calculation P2

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new notes or term debt were issued in fiscal 2025 or in the first nine months of 2026: the three series of senior notes are unchanged since 2021 and the revolving facility is the only material borrowing that moved. The revolver was drawn to fund the 2026 acquisitions of a Cambodian primate supplier and of PathoQuest, which together cost a preliminary $507.3 million and $67.4 million, and it has since been reduced from its first-quarter peak. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-03-28_crl-20260328.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation A8

Two businesses were sold in May 2026: certain European Discovery Services businesses for $126.4 million in cash with up to $10.0 million of contingent payments, and the CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses to GI Partners, where the company paid the buyer net cash of $12.4 million, may fund up to $45.0 million of future losses and capital expenditure over four years and may receive up to $50.0 million of contingent payments valued at $15.7 million. The pre-tax loss on the CDMO and Cell Solutions sale was $181.7 million, recognised in other expense and so outside operating income and EBITDA. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 37

A March 2026 sale of Wilmington property for $60.1 million, with a long-term lease back of some buildings, produced a gain of about $38.5 million inside operating expenses; the lease back adds an operating lease claim that sits outside the debt figure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38

fields.value: Financial foundation for CHARLES RIVER LABORATORIES INTERNATIONAL, INC. (issuer id crl), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway (Full credit assessment). Scope: statements, debt, leverage, cover and liquidity from the 2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three 2026 earnings releases, in US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported net debt is 5.06x LTM EBITDA at the third quarter of 2026, but impairments depress that EBITDA; before them it is 2.61x, so underlying leverage is moderate yet rising, and creditors are exposed to a revolver drawn for acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.32x on an LTM basis, the 2028 notes and the 2029 revolver and notes are the maturities to watch, and contract EBITDA and covenant compliance at the third quarter are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; calculation C19; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, page 152; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage has risen sharply, and two causes are mixed together. Reported total debt to EBITDA went from 3.81x at the 2024 year-end to 4.99x at the 2025 year-end and 5.51x on an LTM basis at the third quarter of 2026, and net debt to EBITDA went from 3.48x to 4.49x and 5.06x. Reported EBITDA fell from USD 589,088 thousand to USD 428,474 thousand in fiscal 2025 mostly because goodwill and long-lived asset impairments rose from USD 266,825 thousand to USD 424,080 thousand, and carrying-value debt then rose by USD 306,825 thousand in the first nine months of 2026 as acquisitions, buybacks and deferred payments exceeded free cash flow and disposal proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-27_crl-20251227.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Before impairments the picture is milder. The house measure adds back the goodwill and long-lived asset impairment lines of the cash flow statement and puts net debt at 2.39x, 2.26x and 2.61x of EBITDA at the same three dates, so underlying leverage rose by about a third of a turn in 2026 where the reported measure rose by more than half a turn. It is an analyst measure, not the issuer's and not the covenant's, and it leaves in a gain of $38.5 million on a Wilmington property sale and a $44.6 million reserve release inside 2026 operating income while leaving out restructuring and deal costs.

fields.value: Interest cover on reported EBITDA is adequate but not wide. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 4.77x in fiscal 2024, 4.21x in fiscal 2025 and 4.32x on an LTM basis, and after capital expenditure the reported ratio is 2.06x for fiscal 2025. The weighted average interest rate on the debt edged up from 4.05% to 4.11% between the 2025 year-end and the third quarter, and cash interest paid was barely higher in the first nine months of 2026, USD 84,528 thousand against USD 83,407 thousand, while the issuer puts the rise in interest expense mainly on non-cash accretion of deferred purchase consideration.

fields.value: Cash generation is solid but is being spent on acquisitions and buybacks faster than it is earned. Operating cash flow was USD 474,887 thousand in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 590,126 thousand a year earlier, lower because of bonus payments and professional fees, and free cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 133,823 thousand was USD 341,064 thousand. Against that, the company paid USD 467,254 thousand for acquisitions, USD 324,105 thousand for share repurchases and USD 111,394 thousand of deferred and contingent consideration, and received USD 176,563 thousand from disposals, so the revolver absorbed the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported liquidity is cash of USD 200,381 thousand plus undrawn revolver commitments of USD 1,056,826 thousand, but usable liquidity is lower. Restricted cash of USD 48,700 thousand is excluded from cash, letters of credit of $21.7 million may or may not use the facility and the facility's leverage and cover tests may constrain drawing, and the sources do not say either way. The revolver was drawn to USD 1,165,073 thousand at the first quarter and has since been reduced to USD 943,174 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of CHARLES RIVER LABORATORIES INTERNATIONAL, INC. (issuer id crl), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway (Full credit assessment). Scope: business, operating model, ownership, transactions, governance and sponsor-type behaviour from the 2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three 2026 earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Charles River is a broad, client-diversified research services group whose 2026 portfolio reshuffle, driven by a board strategic review that followed a cooperation agreement with a large shareholder, makes its capital allocation the main governance question for creditors, although the files show no creditor-adverse conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is medium on the evidence read: no client is above 4% of revenue and regulatory inquiries closed in 2025, but a $1.0 billion repurchase programme, revolver-funded acquisitions and unquantified litigation sit beside loan documents and a proxy statement that were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified by client and geography, and its demand risk is cyclical rather than concentrated. No client accounted for more than 4% of 2025 revenue and none for more than 8% of any segment, the discovery and safety assessment segment generated 59.8% of revenue, research models and services 21.1% and manufacturing 19.1%, and the United States provided 53.34% of revenue. The same segment lost revenue in 2025 as biopharma R&D spending stayed cautious, its backlog slipped to $1.9 billion at the year-end and has since recovered to $2.0 billion, so earnings depend on client funding rather than on any single customer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The portfolio is being reshaped, and the reshaping is the largest 2026 change for creditors. In 2026 the company agreed a preliminary $507.3 million for a Cambodian primate supplier, took full control of PathoQuest for total consideration of $67.4 million, sold certain European Discovery Services businesses to IQVIA for $126.4 million and sold its CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses to GI Partners, paying the buyer net cash of $12.4 million and accepting a possible funding obligation of up to $45.0 million. The sales remove the CDMO and Cell Solutions asset groups that caused the fiscal 2025 intangible impairment of about $211.0 million, and the supplier purchase vertically integrates a constrained input, but the acquisitions were funded from cash and the revolver, so the net effect on creditors depends on how the revolver is repaid and on what is bought next.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder influence is documented, but its financial consequence for creditors is not yet visible in a debt-funded distribution. A cooperation agreement with a large shareholder in May 2025 put a board committee in charge of a strategic review, which in November 2025 set priorities of acquisitions, partnerships, disposal of non-core assets equal to about 7% of 2025 revenue, cost efficiency and a balanced use of cash between acquisitions, buybacks and debt repayment. The company has paid no common dividends, repurchased $350.0 million of shares in 2025 and $300.0 million in the first nine months of 2026 with $700.0 million of a $1.0 billion authorisation left and no programme purchases in the third quarter, and the share count fell 2.66% between January and October 2026, so buybacks are the lever to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leadership has turned over in the roles that matter to lenders, and the files give no cause for concern beyond continuity risk. The chief executive and chair succession was set for 2026-05-05 and the quarterly reports from May 2026 are signed by a new chief executive, the board named an interim chief financial officer in October 2025, the 2025 annual report was signed by that interim officer and the 2026 quarterly reports by a permanent one, and nine of eleven directors are independent with fully independent audit, pay and governance committees. The date of the chief financial officer change is not stated in the files read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory risk has narrowed but litigation risk has not closed. The Department of Justice closed its primate import investigations in August 2025 and the SEC enforcement staff told the company on 2025-11-14 that it did not intend to recommend action, after a charge of $27 million in fiscal 2024 that wrote an inventory of imported primates down to zero, yet the securities class action was partly revived on appeal in August 2025, a second amended complaint was filed on 2026-09-15 and the company moved to dismiss on 2026-10-15, with the plaintiff's answer due 2026-11-16. The company cannot estimate a possible loss, so the claim is an unquantified contingent liability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Restructuring is a recurring cost, not a one-off, and it consumes cash while it lifts margins. The company expects about $300 million of cumulative annualised savings by the end of 2026, announced a further programme in September 2026 intended to save more than $300 million between 2027 and 2030, and booked restructuring charges of $99.8 million in fiscal 2025, $107.0 million in fiscal 2024 and $73.8 million in the first nine months of 2026. Repeated charges mean restructuring spend should be treated as part of running costs when judging free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supply of primates is a single point of failure that the company is addressing by integration. The annual report lists dependence on a limited source of supply for its primate offerings as an industry risk, and the January 2026 acquisition of a Cambodian supplier brings part of that supply in house, which lowers the interruption risk but adds exposure to the same regulators and to deferred consideration, of which about $5 million was unpaid at the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk view is the pace and funding of change: the two 2026 acquisitions cost a combined $574.7 million at preliminary prices, a shareholder-led review is still running, the unused repurchase authorisation of $700.0 million is large against cash, and the revolver peaked at the first quarter before divestiture proceeds arrived. If management were to complete a large acquisition or resume buybacks while the revolver is drawn, creditor-adverse risk would be the better reading. Evidence that points the other way is the repayment of the revolver after the sales, no dividends, closed regulatory inquiries and independent board committees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new notes or term debt were issued in fiscal 2025 or in the first nine months of 2026: the three series of senior notes are unchanged since 2021 and the revolving facility is the only material borrowing that moved. The revolver was drawn to fund the 2026 acquisitions of a Cambodian primate supplier and of PathoQuest, which together cost a preliminary $507.3 million and $67.4 million, and it has since been reduced from its first-quarter peak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two businesses were sold in May 2026: certain European Discovery Services businesses for $126.4 million in cash with up to $10.0 million of contingent payments, and the CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses to GI Partners, where the company paid the buyer net cash of $12.4 million, may fund up to $45.0 million of future losses and capital expenditure over four years and may receive up to $50.0 million of contingent payments valued at $15.7 million. The pre-tax loss on the CDMO and Cell Solutions sale was $181.7 million, recognised in other expense and so outside operating income and EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A March 2026 sale of Wilmington property for $60.1 million, with a long-term lease back of some buildings, produced a gain of about $38.5 million inside operating expenses; the lease back adds an operating lease claim that sits outside the debt figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by shareholder-led buybacks and revolver-funded acquisitions, because cash returned and borrowed for growth slows deleveraging, which implies slower deleveraging and thinner protection for creditors; countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends, closed regulatory inquiries and independent committees.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis of CHARLES RIVER LABORATORIES INTERNATIONAL, INC. (issuer id crl), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway (Full credit assessment). Scope: business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers drawn from the 2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports, the three 2026 earnings releases and the earlier module outputs, in US dollars. No rating, relative value, legal capacity or portfolio sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Charles River is a diversified, cash-generative research services group with an adequate but not strong credit profile: net leverage is 2.61x on EBITDA before impairments but 5.06x as reported, and revolver-funded acquisitions and buybacks leave creditors dependent on management's financial policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand has turned, with organic revenue growth of 4.7% in the third quarter, and free cash flow could repay the drawn revolver of USD 943,174 thousand in 2.36 years, but covenant headroom, ratings and market access are not established, so the view is adequate rather than comfortable. It would improve if free cash flow went to the revolver and weaken if buybacks resumed while the revolver stays drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The recovery in demand is real and is led by the largest segment, so the operating trend now supports credit quality. Organic revenue growth moved from down 1.5% in the first quarter to up 0.1% in the second and up 4.7% in the third, discovery and safety assessment grew 5.9% organically in the third quarter on higher regulated study volume, its backlog rose to $2.0 billion from $1.9 billion at the year-end, and management raised its 2026 organic growth guidance by 150 basis points in August and by 100 basis points in November. Management attributes the third-quarter non-GAAP operating margin of 23.0%, against 19.7% a year earlier, to operating leverage on higher study volume and to the sale of the loss-making contract manufacturing business known as CDMO, so some of the gain is portfolio change and not demand. Reported revenue is still guided to fall 1.5% to 2.0% in 2026 because of the May divestitures, and the guidance and backlog are management measures.

fields.value: Underlying earning power is stable but reported earnings are distorted by charges that recur, so neither the reported nor the adjusted measure is a safe anchor on its own. EBITDA before impairments was 21.13% of revenue in FY2024, 21.23% in FY2025 and 21.60% over the last twelve months, while the reported operating margin fell from 5.6% to 0.6% between FY2024 and FY2025, mainly because intangible asset impairments of USD 210,974 thousand arrived on top of goodwill impairments of USD 215,000 thousand in FY2024 and USD 165,000 thousand in FY2025. Restructuring charges of $107.0 million, $99.8 million and $73.8 million in FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026 show that cost programmes are a running cost, and 2026 operating income also holds a $38.5 million property gain and a $44.6 million reserve release, together $83.1 million or 18.78% of nine-month operating income, that will not repeat.

In the first nine months of 2026 free cash flow fell 25.84% to USD 341,064 thousand on bonus payments and professional fees, and cash paid for income taxes fell by USD 57,048 thousand to USD 35,643 thousand, which helped operating cash flow; whether the lower tax payments repeat is not established.

fields.value: Financial policy is the main credit risk, because 2026 spending on acquisitions and buybacks has outrun free cash flow. In the first nine months free cash flow of USD 341,064 thousand covered only 37.78% of the USD 902,753 thousand spent on acquisitions, deferred consideration and buybacks, disposal and insurance proceeds filled part of the gap, the revolver rose from USD 616,503 thousand at the year-end to USD 943,174 thousand after a first-quarter peak of USD 1,165,073 thousand, and net debt rose USD 320,214 thousand. In FY2025 buybacks of $350.0 million were 67.50% of free cash flow, so the change is the acquisition programme. Net leverage on EBITDA before impairments rose from 2.26x to 2.61x, all $300.0 million of programme buybacks were made in the first two quarters, and $700.0 million of authorisation remains, so resumption while the revolver is drawn is the event that would turn this finding into a downgrade of the view.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and no material debt falls due before fiscal 2028, so the credit test is the 2028 to 2029 refinancing and not the next twelve months. Cash of USD 200,381 thousand and undrawn revolver commitments of USD 1,056,826 thousand give USD 1,257,207 thousand, or USD 1,235,507 thousand if the $21.7 million of letters of credit use the facility, and the ladder printed at the year-end shows only USD 2,883 thousand of principal before fiscal 2028. Fiscal 2028 holds the 2028 notes of USD 500,000 thousand and fiscal 2029 holds the revolver and the 2029 notes at USD 1,443,174 thousand, which is 1.68x EBITDA before impairments. The weighted average interest rate is 4.11% and the three series of notes carry fixed coupons of 4.25%, 3.75% and 4.00%, while the revolver margin is set by the leverage ratio, so rising leverage raises its cost; the files give no rating or market yield, so the cost of refinancing the notes is not established.

fields.value: The covenant tests cannot be turned into headroom, and reported ratios conflict with the stated compliance. The credit agreement requires EBITDA less capital expenditure to cash interest of at least 3.50x and debt to EBITDA of no more than 4.25x on contract definitions, and the company stated compliance at 2025-12-27. On reported EBITDA the ratios at that date were 2.06x and 4.99x, outside both levels, so contract EBITDA must add back items such as impairments by an amount the files do not give, and no compliance statement is printed for 2026. Availability of the revolver, which is secured on substantially all assets of the company, is therefore the main dependency of the liquidity view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competition, animal-testing policy and primate supply cap growth and pricing but do not threaten near-term cash flow. The company competes with the in-house resources of its clients and with described rivals in each segment, many contracts are fixed price or capped fee-for-service so overruns fall on the company, and in many cases it is owed no termination fee if a client cancels. The FDA announced in April 2025 that it would expand the use of new approach methodologies in preclinical safety studies and the company describes the move away from animal testing as gradual over many years, while primate supply rests on a limited source that the January 2026 Cambodian acquisition partly internalises. These risks lower the quality of the revenue base slowly, and in FY2025 a 2.0% fall in discovery and safety assessment revenue cost 37.10% of the lost revenue in segment operating income, a figure that includes higher restructuring charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are moderate against cash flow, but they add fixed charges that sit ahead of equity. Operating lease commitments were $626.6 million at the year-end with $80.7 million due within twelve months, unconditional purchase obligations were about $340 million, the company may fund up to $45.0 million of losses and capital expenditure of the divested CDMO business, the Noveprim minority holders hold a put carried at USD 43,173 thousand, and the net pension and supplemental plan liability was USD 32,170 thousand. None is in the debt figure, so lease and purchase commitments should be read with interest cover of 4.32x on reported EBITDA.

fields.value: Headline 2026 profit overstates cash earnings and should not drive the view. Net income of USD 318,882 thousand for the first nine months includes a non-cash reversal of acquired tax reserves of USD 245,638 thousand, of which $44.6 million sits in operating income and about $201 million in the tax line, leaving USD 73,244 thousand, which is itself after a $181.7 million pre-tax loss on the CDMO and Cell Solutions sale that sits in other expense, outside operating income and EBITDA. The credit view therefore rests on cash flow and EBITDA, not on reported earnings per share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate view is on the financial side. Reported total debt to EBITDA of 5.51x over the last twelve months is above the 4.25x covenant ceiling, repeated impairments suggest that earlier acquisitions have not earned their cost, Manufacturing goodwill already carries $380 million of accumulated impairments, and the 2026 programme of acquisitions and buybacks was funded mostly by debt because free cash flow covered only 37.78% of it. If the revolver rises again, or a further impairment lands before the covenant definition is seen, reported leverage becomes the better anchor and the view should move from adequate to weak. The evidence for a stronger view is the demand recovery, a third-quarter margin 330 basis points above the prior year, the sale of a loss-making business, free cash flow of USD 399,634 thousand over the last twelve months and the absence of any material maturity before 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F6; calculation F11; calculation P6; 10-Q_2026-09-26_crl-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 25; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.value: The view would strengthen if free cash flow went to the revolver and buybacks stayed paused until net leverage on EBITDA before impairments fell back to 2.26x, if the compliance certificates and the credit agreement showed ample headroom on the contract definition, or if a rating and market yields showed open access. It would weaken if buybacks resumed or a large acquisition were announced while the revolver is drawn, if organic growth turned negative again, if the backlog of discovery and safety assessment fell below $1.9 billion, or if the 2026 compliance certificates showed tight headroom on the contract definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Five strengths support the view, in order of weight. Demand and backlog are recovering in the largest segment, and semi-fixed laboratory cost means extra volume lifts margin and free cash flow, which supports deleveraging capacity. Client and geographic diversification mean that no client was above 4% of revenue and no client above 8% of any segment, so the loss of one client cannot break cash flow. Free cash flow of USD 518,494 thousand in FY2025 on capital expenditure of 5.46% of revenue funds interest and shareholder returns internally. Liquidity of USD 1,257,207 thousand and the absence of material maturities before 2028 give time to refinance. Management has moved to sell loss-making units and to cut costs, with about $300 million of annualised savings targeted by the end of 2026, which improves the quality of earnings if the savings are realised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Five weaknesses constrain the view, in order of weight. Financial policy has put acquisitions and buybacks ahead of debt reduction, which lifted net leverage on EBITDA before impairments from 2.26x to 2.61x in nine months. Reported total debt to EBITDA of 5.51x and the unresolved gap to the covenant definition leave headroom not calculable. Impairments and restructuring recur, so reported earnings are low in quality. Debt is concentrated in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029, with the revolver, secured on substantially all assets, maturing in December 2029. Regulatory pressure on animal testing, limited primate supply and fixed-price contracts erode pricing power slowly, and the fall in discovery and safety assessment revenue in FY2025 showed that cost does not flex fully.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions of financial profile, scale and market position is Strong because the company states that it is the largest provider in its field and reports USD 4,015,382 thousand of revenue, although market share is not established; business diversification is Strong by client and geography but Average by end market because demand rests on drug research funding; competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability, ability to refinance, liquidity position and financial policy and governance are each Average; none is Weak. Financial policy and governance is the weakest dimension in the sense of the greatest credit uncertainty, because the files show no creditor-adverse conduct but nothing that commits management to deleveraging. The six business quality factors follow the same pattern: revenue durability, margin resilience, free cash flow conversion, liquidity buffer and refinancing capacity are Average and governance and financial policy is Average with a negative bias, and the primary downside path is renewed client funding restraint during the revolver-funded acquisition and buyback programme ahead of the fiscal 2028 to 2029 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Charles River is a US-listed provider of outsourced non-clinical drug discovery, safety assessment, research models and quality-control testing, and the cash flow it generates comes from drug developers that must buy regulated studies and models. Discovery and safety assessment was 59.8% of FY2025 revenue, research models and services 21.1% and manufacturing solutions 19.1%, and the United States provided 53.34% of revenue by operating entity, so cash flow follows pharmaceutical and biotechnology research budgets with a euro, sterling and Canadian dollar overlay. No single client was above 4% of revenue, which limits single-client risk, and the company describes many relationships as long-term, but a services backlog can be cancelled and is not a reliable forecast. The business model supports cash-flow visibility through backlog and contracts that can run for several years and weakens it through fixed-price work and client budget swings, so debt service depends on keeping utilisation high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is publicly listed, has no controlling shareholder or sponsor, has paid no common dividend and is influenced by a large shareholder through a cooperation agreement of May 2025 that put a board committee in charge of a strategic review. The review set acquisitions, disposal of non-core assets, cost efficiency and balanced use of cash among acquisitions, buybacks and debt repayment as priorities, the share count fell as buybacks continued, and the company holds 90% of Noveprim with a put on the other 10% from December 2030. Ownership therefore adds buyback and acquisition pressure but no sponsor leakage, and creditors rely on board independence and the revolver's covenants for protection; the files supply no ownership percentages, standstill terms or guarantor structure, and no controlling shareholder is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and discretionary, not recurring: study volumes follow client research budgets, which fell in 2024 and 2025 and are recovering in 2026. In FY2025 service revenue fell 1.6% and product revenue rose 2.6%, discovery and safety assessment revenue fell 2.0% on lower study volume while research models rose on large-model volume and small-model pricing, and the manufacturing segment lost CDMO customers. Remaining performance obligations on contracts of more than a year were $675.3 million with about 60% due within twelve months, up from about 50% at the year-end, so the multi-year contracted book is only a part of revenue and the larger backlog includes short contracts that the performance obligation figure excludes and that can be cancelled. Revenue durability is Average: diversification across clients is strong, but visibility is short.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are only partly defensible under volume pressure, because cost behaves as semi-fixed. Cost of services was 71.22% of service revenue in FY2025 against 70.99% in FY2024 and 70.54% in the first nine months of 2026, and selling and administrative cost fell from 18.54% of revenue in FY2024 to 17.73% in nine months 2026 while the savings programme progressed. In FY2025 the lost discovery and safety assessment revenue of USD 48,389 thousand was offset by only USD 11,149 thousand of lower cost of revenue, so 37.10% of it reached segment operating income, a figure that includes higher restructuring charges. Pass-through is partial: the annual report lists costs rising faster than market prices in certain businesses as a risk, says the cost of collecting, processing and testing products has risen significantly in recent years and that fixed-price contracts limit the ability to hold margins, while small research model pricing rose in FY2025 and lower sourcing cost for large research models helped the third-quarter margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and partly flexible, and the main drains on cash are discretionary or one-off. Capital expenditure was 5.75% of revenue in FY2024, 5.46% in FY2025 and 4.49% in the first nine months of 2026, income taxes paid were $119.6 million in FY2025, and cash interest was USD 102,839 thousand over the last twelve months. Restructuring cash, bonuses, acquisition spending and buybacks absorb the rest, and the files do not split maintenance and growth capital expenditure, so the flexibility is not quantified. EBITDA before impairments converted to free cash flow at 58.61% in FY2024 and 60.82% in FY2025, which is enough to service the debt and repay the revolver over time if distributions are restrained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense, and the company states that it is the largest provider in a regulated field. Safety assessment has dozens of competitors with two main ones, discovery has hundreds with two main ones, research models has four and microbial testing has four, and clients can also use internal resources, so price and capacity compete with service quality, and fixed-price contracts transfer cost overruns to the company; this limits margin upside, and the files give no data on switching costs, client retention or entry barriers, so the durability of share is not established and any view that new entrants are limited is an analyst inference from regulation and capital intensity. The threat of substitutes is rising slowly: the FDA announced expanded use of new approach methodologies in April 2025 and the United Kingdom published a roadmap in November 2025, and the company is building such methods itself, so substitution would shift revenue from animal studies to other services rather than remove it, which is an analyst inference. Buyer power is high collectively because large clients seek lower research cost per drug candidate and many contracts allow termination without a fee, yet low single-client concentration limits any one buyer. Supplier power was high for primates, with a pricing environment the annual report calls extremely dynamic, and eased in 2026 as the company bought a Cambodian supplier and reported lower sourcing cost for large research models.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: External factors matter to credit in four ways. Regulation of animal use and of primate imports can interrupt supply or cut demand, and the company booked a $27 million primate inventory charge in fiscal 2024 that has since been partly reversed as animals were used. Trade policy, including tariffs, is listed as a risk to costs and supply. Currency matters because a 10% stronger dollar would have cut nine-month 2026 revenue by $135.8 million and operating income by $33.2 million, against a $9.6 million gain on the same test for FY2025, so the profit sensitivity changed sign and the reason is not stated. Funding conditions for biotechnology clients, which the company says improved in 2026, are the dominant economic driver of demand. Technology adds a cost lever through automation and digital pathology but also the new methods that substitute for animal work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are client diversification, the recovering backlog, moderate capital intensity, distant maturities and a cost programme; the weaknesses are the revolver-funded acquisition and buyback programme, recurring impairments, concentrated 2028 to 2029 maturities, fixed-price contract risk and reliance on one limited primate supply chain. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the vertical integration of primate supply, the sale of loss-making units, savings of more than $300 million between 2027 and 2030 and an adjustment of capital allocation toward debt reduction. Threats that could weaken it are a relapse in client funding, a faster move away from animal testing, a primate supply interruption and a large debt-funded acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the balance of evidence is positive for operations and neutral for leverage. Tailwinds are the discovery and safety assessment backlog of $2.0 billion, bookings and proposals that the company calls robust, the highest net book-to-bill in nearly four years reported for the second quarter, a guidance path that has risen in each of the last two releases, the sale of loss-making CDMO operations and cost savings that are meant to reach about $300 million annualised by the end of 2026. Headwinds are revenue lost to the divestitures, weaker research model demand with organic revenue down 0.6% in the third quarter, restructuring charges for the Create the Future programme, payments of deferred acquisition consideration, and cash taxes that were unusually low in 2026 and may rise. The credit consequence is better EBITDA and free cash flow, which helps deleveraging only if distributions are restrained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years, the main issues are the substitution of animal studies, the pace of the cost programme and the refinancing of USD 1,943,174 thousand of notes and revolver that fall due in fiscal 2028 and 2029. Management expects incremental savings of more than $300 million between 2027 and 2030 and the sale of non-core assets of about 7% of 2025 revenue, which together could raise margins and cut scale. The credit consequence is that refinancing is likely to be manageable if free cash flow is applied to the revolver before 2028, and harder if debt-funded acquisitions continue; the files provide no medium-term leverage target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most credible downside combines the client funding squeeze the company has already lived through with a continuing programme of revolver-funded acquisitions and buybacks. The initiating condition is renewed restraint in biopharma and biotechnology research budgets, such as the 2024 to 2025 period when discovery and safety assessment revenue fell 2.0% and the backlog slipped from $2.0 billion to $1.9 billion. The first operational break is lower study starts and cancellations in discovery and safety assessment, where cost behaves as semi-fixed and 37.10% of lost revenue reached segment operating income in FY2025 including restructuring charges. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA and free cash flow, with restructuring charges and fixed-price overruns adding cash costs; in the earlier downturn free cash flow still held at USD 501,610 thousand in FY2024 and USD 518,494 thousand in FY2025, so the cash base proved resilient. The liquidity and leverage consequence depends on policy: if buybacks and acquisitions continue while free cash flow falls, the revolver of USD 943,174 thousand would rise again, net leverage would exceed 2.61x on EBITDA before impairments, and reported leverage would stay above the 4.25x covenant ceiling with contract headroom unseen. Management levers are suspension of the $700.0 million buyback programme, lower capital expenditure, slower acquisitions and further cost cuts, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis because USD 1,257,207 thousand of liquidity is available and no maturity falls before 2028, provided the revolver can be drawn. The observable triggers are discovery and safety assessment backlog below $1.9 billion, organic growth turning negative again, revolver borrowing rising while organic growth is weak, and any change in the covenant disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second path is a supply or regulatory shock, such as a primate import restriction or an acceleration of animal-testing reform. The first break would be a halt to studies or a drop in volume, the transmission would be lower revenue with fixed laboratory cost, and the consequence would be a slower recovery than management guides; the files do not quantify this path and it is smaller in the near term than the funding path.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Charles River presents an adequate business profile supported by client diversification, a recovering backlog, moderate capital intensity and a cost programme, but credit quality is constrained by revolver-funded acquisitions and buybacks, recurring impairments and an unresolved gap between reported leverage and the covenant definition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow held at USD 501,610 thousand and USD 518,494 thousand through the 2024 to 2025 downturn and converted 58.61% and 60.82% of EBITDA before impairments in those years. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the use of free cash flow to reduce the revolver before the fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 maturities and on market access that no rating or yield in the files confirms. The primary downside path is renewed client funding restraint while distributions and acquisitions continue to be funded on the revolver. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and compliance certificates, a rating or market yields, management's leverage and cash flow targets and the revenue split between large pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients. Top risk: financial policy that lets net debt rise faster than earnings recover.
